newsitem.title: CANADA: GM shuts down two Canadian plants - CP.
newsitem.headline: GM shuts down two Canadian plants - CP.

text.p: General Motors Corp shut down two of its Canadian assembly plants in Oshawa as a result of a strike at its transmission plant in Warren, Michigan, the Canadian Press news agency reported on Thursday.
The Canadian Press said that about 3,000 workers were sidelined because there were no parts to build the Buicks and Chevrolets that usually roll off the assembly lines.
"We have told our Plant One and Plant Two workers not to show up," CP quoted GM spokesman Charles McGregor as saying.
GM Canada officials could not be reached for comment.
CP reported that 3,800 other autoworkers at GM's giant manufacturing complex in Oshawa, just east of Toronto, could be out of work if the Michigan strike was not settled by Friday night.
The GM truck plant in Oshawa was unaffected.
About 2,800 workers from United Auto Worker Local 909 struck the Warren engine component plant when contract talks did not produce a new agreement.

The Warren plant supplies four-speed automatic transmissions for front-wheel-drive cars vehicles. It also makes suspension control arms and wheels. A lengthy strike could seriously disrupt GM's North American production, analysts have said.
